claims.text: EF Core docs: relationships are defined by foreign keys, and navigations are layered over them to provide an object-oriented view; a navigation property does not replace the foreign key property, both can coexist on the same entity.

EF Core docs: HasMany(...).WithOne() and HasOne(...).WithMany() are equivalent starting points for configuring the same one-to-many relationship, each paired with HasForeignKey(...) naming the foreign key property.

EF Core docs: a collection navigation (e.g. Order.Items) and a reference navigation (e.g. OrderItem back to Order) are each optional parts of a relationship; a relationship can be configured with a navigation on only one side.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, entity-framework/core/modeling/relationships/one-to-many.md ("Optionally, a collection navigation...", "Optionally, a reference navigation...")

claims.text: EF Core docs: multiple properties can be configured as an entity's key together, known as a composite key, via HasKey(x => new { x.A, x.B }); this exact anonymous-type syntax is EF Core's own documented example.

Order (DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs) has both CustomerId (int) and Customer (Customer?, a navigation property) as separate properties, plus Items (List<OrderItem>); OrderItem has no Id property at all, only OrderId, ProductId, Quantity, UnitPriceVnd.

DonHangDbContext.OnModelCreating configures Order.Items via e.HasMany(o => o.Items).WithOne().HasForeignKey(i => i.OrderId), Order.Customer via e.HasOne(o => o.Customer).WithMany().HasForeignKey(o => o.CustomerId), and OrderItem's composite key via e.HasKey(i => new { i.OrderId, i.ProductId }).
OrderItem has no property referencing Order, and Customer has no property listing its orders, so both WithOne() and WithMany() in this codebase are called with no argument.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang/DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs at tag stage-1 (full file: OrderItem and Customer classes)

claims.text: A reference navigation is a free-choice nullable only when its FK property is non-nullable (must be nullable if the FK property is). Optional vs required is governed by the FK property, not the column, unless IsRequired/[Required] overrides it.
EF Core identifies one row of a composite-key entity by all key parts together; Find takes every key value, in the order HasKey declares them.

EF Core configures a property named Id or <type name>Id as the primary key by convention, and conventions set up a composite key only in special cases (like an owned type collection), so OrderItem needs an explicit HasKey.
db/schema.sql at stage-1 declares order_items with PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id) and orders.customer_id as integer NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (id).
